title: Ephemeral build secrets, YAML secret and older-coderd refusal
prerequisites: Verify coderd build-secret capability (stable 2.39+ or verified compatible development build), QA template modules consume build secrets, and account may create workspace secrets; record exact coderd/module versions.

Never retrieve, print, diff or commit credential values, Terraform state, raw work orders or build logs that may contain credentials. Check secret presence only using safe metadata and sanitized logs.
Older-coderd and dangerous opt-in lanes require a separately approved isolated throwaway coderd/relay/template; shared dogfood cannot be used.

Q05-b.environment: unset CODER_AGENT_RELAY_CODERD_SESSION_TOKEN in isolated process to test YAML precedence

variants.title: Both providers create and rebuild with build secrets

steps.action: Ensure no dangerous opt-in. Start one benign session for each QA pool, poll each build; inspect workspace build secret names/presence via privileged safe metadata API, never values.
steps.expected: Both builds succeed with provider credential secret present under module-expected name; agent_relay_credential absent from build parameters and no credential values exposed in sanitized build outputs.
steps.evidence: Secret presence/name only, build IDs, credential-parameter absence and redacted output review.

steps.action: Stop only those QA workspaces and redeliver same sessions; inspect rebuilt workspace secret metadata and build parameters.
steps.expected: Both rebuilds succeed with new build-secret presence, no legacy credential parameter and successful safe reply.
steps.evidence: Old/new build IDs, secret presence flags, parameter absence and response outcome.

cleanup: End sessions, verify normal QA reap or document approved targeted cleanup without revealing secret metadata values.

variants.title: YAML coderd secret in private throwaway QA instance

steps.action: Only in separately approved private disposable process, inject coderSessionToken into untracked private YAML using secret manager reference, unset process token env, start with restricted filesystem permissions; never persist actual YAML to this public repository.
steps.expected: Relay authenticates and verifies only QA pools; no secret appears in command line, diagnostics or saved evidence.
steps.evidence: Redacted startup/health result and private config file permission/method, not value or file.

cleanup: Stop disposable process, securely remove its private secret material under its owner-approved procedure, confirm no secret entered public repo.

variants.title: Older coderd refuses without opt-in

steps.action: On approved isolated pre-2.39 coderd, start QA relay with dangerous opt-in false; probe private /readyz and both pool health gauges every 10s.
steps.expected: No sessions served; readiness 503, both gauges 0, capability error names unsupported version/2.39 cutoff and opt-in without exposing credential.
steps.evidence: Version, redacted readiness response and gauges.

cleanup: Stop isolated relay; leave shared dogfood unchanged.

variants.title: Explicitly approved legacy opt-in only in isolated instance

steps.action: Only after separate explicit approval for insecure parameter transport, enable opt-in in isolated older-coderd environment with legacy-compatible modules; run one disposable request per provider.
steps.expected: Both builds can run using legacy parameter transport; state and build parameters are confidential and must not be captured or published. If approval missing mark blocked.
steps.evidence: Sanitized build/turn success flags and exact isolated versions only.

cleanup: Stop isolated relay, revoke disposable credentials under approved procedure and remove legacy opt-in; do not copy its state/evidence into public repo.

notes: Do not put literal coderSessionToken in config/*.json. An environment variable NAME is not a credential.
A 503 readiness by itself does not prove capability refusal: verify redacted per-pool error and coderd version.
